resources.string: The first time, Android asks you to allow installing apps from DualSub Replay. Your saved words and settings stay.
Installing… The app closes while it updates.
This copy of the app was built on a computer, so it can\'t update itself. Get the latest version on GitHub.
Couldn\'t reach GitHub. Check your connection and try again.
GitHub is busy right now. Try again in a few minutes.
GitHub sent an unexpected answer. Try again later.
The download didn\'t match GitHub\'s checksum, so it was deleted.
The download isn\'t a newer version of this app, so it wasn\'t installed.
Once a day when you open the app, checks GitHub for a new version, downloads it on Wi-Fi and installs it when you leave the app, never while a video plays.
This copy of the app can\'t update itself.

Once a day when you open the app, reads a small file on GitHub to learn about new versions and temporary fixes for YouTube or Google changes. Nothing about you or your videos is sent. When off, the app asks GitHub only when you tap Check for updates.
Version %1$s fixes a security problem in the version you have (%2$s). Update now? Your saved words and settings stay.
While this is off, you won\'t hear about new versions or security updates.

For finding why Bluetooth sound distorts, drops out or repeats. Each stage keeps the ones above it. Play a video for about 10 minutes on a stage, then try the next one. Subtitles may lag or stop from stage 3 on.
Full screen works as before the screen-off fix of v1.8.15. The sound may stop briefly when the screen turns off in full screen.
Stage 1, and no media notification and nothing sent to the earphones about the video. Earphone buttons and screen-off playing stop working; test with the screen on.
Stage 2, and the page is read once a second instead of 10 times a second. Subtitles move in jumps.
Stage 3, and none of the app\'s repeating page scripts run (subtitles, captions, ad skipping, study tools). Subtitles stop moving.
Stage 4, and the page is loaded again without anything the app adds to it, as close to YouTube in Chrome as the app can get.
When you hear a glitch, note the time, open this page and send a screenshot of the log. Lines with "page:" are what the video did; "app:" lines are what the app asked for.
